newsitem.title: USA: Koch pipeline still closed, reopen date unclear.
newsitem.headline: Koch pipeline still closed, reopen date unclear.

text.p: A Koch Oil pipeline damaged by an explosion in Texas last month will remain closed until the cause of the accident is determined, the company said Wednesday.
"We want to make certain that we fully understand what happened with the pipeline," said Koch spokesman Riff Yeager, adding the company's major concern is the community's safety.
The Aug 24 explosion on the 35,000 barrel per day capacity line killed two teen-agers in Lively, Texas, a small town 40 miles southeast of Dalls.
Police initially speculated the explosion occurred due to a leak of normal butane from the pipeline that was ignited when the teen-agers tried to start up their car.

Yeager said Koch has been working with the National Transportation Safety Board to determine the cause of the accident. But, he could not give an estimate as to when the cause would be determined and the line reopened.
The pipeline is the smaller of two lines along the Koch Sterling system that feeds industrial customers in the Gulf Coast from storage facilities in Mont Belvieu, Texas.
Since the explosion, flow along the larger, 100,000 bpd capacity line, has been increased.
